title: Like a Rogue
description: Count safe tiles in a cellular automaton where traps spread based on the left and right neighbours of the previous row.
writeup:
## Approach

The four trap rules from the puzzle all share a common structure: a new tile is a trap if and only if its **left and right neighbours in the previous row differ** (one trap, one safe). The centre tile is irrelevant. This simplifies the rule to a single XOR:

```
new[i] = '^'  if  prev[i-1] ≠ prev[i+1]  else  '.'
```

With the row encoded as an integer bitmask (bit `i` = 1 means trap), the entire next row can be computed in two shifts and an XOR:

```python
row = ((row << 1) ^ (row >> 1)) & mask
```

This is O(1) per row regardless of width, and Python's arbitrary-precision integers handle any row length without extra work.

## Part 1

Simulate 40 rows, summing `width - popcount(row)` (safe count) each step.

## Part 2

Same loop for 400,000 rows. The bitmask approach makes this fast enough to run in a couple of seconds even in Python — no numpy or other libraries needed.
